correctness.rationale: Exact two-step directed-ball decomposition Q_c union R_(b,c) union {abc}; forced-word pair (abc,cbc) has singleton symmetric difference; nonbinary sufficiency proven by exhausting c-different, b-different, a-different cases, with strict q(q-1)>q and q-1>=2. Binary forced extras and two size-seven solutions checked with explicit signatures; incoming convention follows by word reversal. Two standalone direct-neighborhood programs passed for q=2..9 (outgoing) and q=2..7 (incoming). Finite tests are corroboration, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: Addresses the shortest exceptional word length n=2t-1=3 for radius-two identification specifically omitted from the archival theorem, proving a sharp alphabet transition q=2 vs q>=3 and classifying every optimal directed identifying code in an infinite alphabet family. The uniqueness is structurally stronger than the previously known generic size lower bound and relevant to deterministic sensor placement in directed sequence networks; no speculative downstream theorem is claimed.
